alfway to Heaven begins and ends in the Town of
istol, commonly referred to as “The Gateway to the
een Mountains.” This loop takes you from Bristol
ong Route 116/17 to the Lincoln Road, where you
ll travel uphill alongside the New Haven River. After
ssing through the center of Lincoln, the incline will
crease somewhat but then level off. At this point you’ll
leaving paved roads to a dirt road with a variety
uphill, downhill and flat sections. Upon reaching
rusalem, you’ll be back again on paved roads, which
ing you down a steep hill until you once again reach
ute 116/17, bringing you to a level road as you return
Bristol center. Halfway to Heaven showcases a
brant downtown, historic buildings, beautiful rivers and
ountain views, and a landscape that was dramatically
anged in places because of a large flood.

is loop leads from Vergennes, Vermont’s oldest and
allest city, through villages and rich farmland, to
istol, the “Gateway to the Green Mountains,” and back
ain. Vergennes and Bristol both have charming,
storic downtowns with inviting shops and restaurants.
t Good Food in Vergennes is popular with bicyclists,
d the Bristol Bakery on Main Street and seasonal
llage Cremee Stand on the outskirts of Bristol should
t be missed.
is route runs along mainly paved roads with dirt
ctions of Hardscrabble Road and Plank Road. Cyclists
ould be in good shape to tackle this fairly hilly loop,
t note that there are places in Vergennes, Monkton
d Bristol to get off your bicycle and rest, eat and drink
ong the way.
